standard_prerequisites.use: Applied to the sequence formed by the kernel and cokernel of $f$, it expresses $e_R(M, \varphi, \psi)$ as the sum of $e_R(M', \varphi', \psi')$ and the multiplicities of the two end terms.

standard_prerequisites.name: Vanishing of the multiplicity for a periodic complex with finite length cohomology
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, label lemma-finite-periodic-length (invoked at proof line 294)
standard_prerequisites.use: It shows that the kernel and the cokernel, being of finite length and with finite length cohomology, contribute zero.

core_obligations: Apply additivity of the multiplicity to the map of periodic complexes, splitting it into the kernel and the cokernel (proof line 291).

Observe that $(\Ker(f), \varphi, \psi)$ and $(\Coker(f), \varphi', \psi')$ have vanishing multiplicity, by the finite length statement, since the kernel and cokernel have finite length by hypothesis (proof lines 292-294).
Conclude the equality of the two multiplicities (proof lines 284-287).
proof_roadmap: Additivity applied to the kernel and cokernel (proof line 291).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a map of $(2,1)$-periodic complexes whose kernel and cokernel have finite length preserves the multiplicity, provided the cohomology modules have finite length (statement lines 282-288). The proof splits the map through its kernel and cokernel using additivity of the multiplicity and then kills the two end terms through the vanishing criterion for finite length cohomology. The two-step reduction is the substance, so the claim is H2.
